items.name: radio/hiphop/01-on-the-air
items.title: Killfeed Says You're On The Air
items.prompt: Boom bap hip hop, calm braggadocio, mid 90s dusty sampler era, 92 BPM, A minor. Chopped break, fat kick, upright bass loop, filtered horn stab, scratch hook. Male rapper, laid back and precise, clear diction. Intro: radio static and a station drop. Verse one on drums and bass. Chorus with horn stab and scratched cuts: "Killfeed says you're on the air". Verse two adds muted keys. Bridge: bare drums and a spoken aside. Final chorus doubled, tape stop ending. Lyrics: DJ Mega Colony welcomes callers to Perim Ghost, spectators in the booth and joiners on the air, the running gag is the killfeed as the on air light. Objects: a headset, a chain link fence, a coolant puddle. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/02-not-for-public-release
items.title: Not For Public Release
items.prompt: G-funk hip hop, smooth and sunny with a smirk, early 90s West Coast era, 96 BPM, G minor. Whining portamento lead synth, deep live bass, slow funk drums, electric keyboard stabs, female talkbox hook. Male rapper, unhurried and cocky, clear diction. Intro: lead synth melody over bass. Verse one rides the groove. Chorus with talkbox harmonies: "Not for public release". Verse two adds a wah guitar. Breakdown on bass and claps with a stamp thud. Final chorus with layered synth, slow fade. Lyrics: Hangar Candy flechette main Kragge cruises Larak Lot leaving DENIED watermarks on every frag, the running gag is the declassification stamp taunt. Objects: a gloss black triangle, a rubber stamp, a parking ramp. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/03-scout-ant-got-deleted
items.title: Scout Ant Got Deleted
items.prompt: Trap hip hop, dark and playful, modern era, 140 BPM, F minor. Rolling hi hats, booming sub bass, sparse minor plucks, a detuned bell, snare rolls. Male rapper, fast triplet flow with a chanted gang vocal hook, clear diction. Intro: plucks and a whispered count. Verse one with hats and sub. Chorus chanted with layered ad libs: "Scout ant got deleted". Verse two doubles the flow speed. Beat switch to half time with the bell. Final chorus, hard stop. Lyrics: a Flanker called Scout Ant runs three clean frags on Area Kitchen, the running gag is scout ant deleted, that is not a metaphor, or it is. Objects: a sugar packet, a break room fridge, a fluorescent tube. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/04-both-wings-sealed
items.title: Both Wings Sealed, Pipe Stayed Open
items.prompt: Drill hip hop, cold and confident, modern era, 138 BPM, C sharp minor. Sliding sub bass, skippy triplet hi hats, ominous piano, distant choir pad, rimshot snare. Two male rappers trading bars, one gravelly, one nasal, clear diction. Intro: piano and choir pad. Verse one from the first voice. Chorus by both: "Both wings sealed, pipe stayed open". Verse two from the second voice with the bass sliding harder. Bridge with the two voices overlapping. Final chorus, cold stop. Lyrics: Static Kids FL_NKR and RSH__ hold East-West Pipe, zero cover, pure aim, the running gag is the pipe that stayed open after both wings got sealed. Objects: a rusted valve wheel, a sealed wing door, a scatter shell. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/05-crossfader-colony
items.title: Crossfader Colony
items.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Turntablist hip hop on a breakbeat backbone, cocky and busy, late 90s battle DJ era, 118 BPM, D minor. Chopped funk break, rubbery bass, brass stabs, a sitar loop, heavy crossfader scratches used as the lead instrument. Arrangement: intro on the naked break with crackle, then the bass drops. Section one: brass stabs answered by transformer scratches. Section two: the sitar loop takes over while the scratches chop into rhythmic patterns. Breakdown: beat juggling on the drums alone. Final section stacks everything under a long crab scratch solo, then a needle lift ending. Mood: DJ Mega Colony's desk theme for The Lot, ant war swagger with no words.

items.name: radio/hiphop/06-tickets-pay-the-frequency
items.title: Tickets Pay The Frequency
items.prompt: Jazz rap, warm and wry, early 90s jazz sampling era, 95 BPM, E flat major. Brushed drums, walking upright bass, muted trumpet, electric piano chords, vinyl crackle. Female rapper, conversational and witty, clear diction. Intro: trumpet and bass. Verse one over the full band. Chorus sung softly with trumpet answers: "Tickets pay the frequency". Verse two with piano comping and a scat ad lib. Trumpet solo over the changes. Final chorus with the band swelling, gentle ride out. Lyrics: an agent called Hermes explains the ticket economy on Diego Far, tickets buy your turn in the fight, and the gossip is who Hermes, Pi, and L5 are trading with. Objects: a paper ticket roll, a dusty scope lens, a stapler. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/07-larak-lot-special
items.title: Larak Lot Special
items.prompt: Southern bounce hip hop, rowdy and grinning, late 90s block party era, 100 BPM, B flat major. Chopped brass fanfare, hand claps, drum machine kicks, a whistle, crowd chants. Male rapper shouting call and response with a crowd, clear diction. Intro: whistle and claps. Verse one over the brass loop. Chorus chanted with the crowd: "Larak Lot special, run it back". Verse two with a bass drop. Breakdown of claps and chants with a spoken procurement sign off. Final chorus, brass blast, air horn. Lyrics: procurement officer Larak signed for every gun in the building, five levels of ramps and Scatter, the running gag is the Host calling it the Larak Lot special when frags spike. Objects: a parking stub, a boom gate arm, a flickering level sign. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/08-alpha-seven-niner-tango
items.title: Alpha Seven Niner Tango
items.prompt: Lo-fi hip hop with vocals, sleepy and paranoid, late 2010s bedroom tape era, 89 BPM, E minor. Dusty piano loop, soft round kick, tape hiss, shortwave static, a faint Morse blip. Male vocalist, half sung and half rapped, close mic and gentle, clear diction. Intro: shortwave static and the piano loop. Verse one over piano and drums. Chorus sung like a lullaby: "Alpha seven, niner tango". Verse two adds a warm bass. Interlude of numbers read quietly. Final chorus, tape slows to a stop. Lyrics: a believer callsigned Crackpot on Chemtrail Alley reads spawn weather digits as poetry, the running gag is numbers station weather that nobody understands. Objects: a rooftop duct, a shortwave radio, a contrail that does not move. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/09-ten-in-the-box
items.title: Ten In The Box
items.prompt: Crunk hip hop, aggressive and huge, mid 2000s Southern club era, 134 BPM with a half time feel, F sharp minor. Distorted sub bass, brass synth stabs, marching snare rolls, gang vocal chants, a siren. Male rapper shouting with crowd response, clear diction. Intro: siren and a shouted count. Verse one over the brass stabs. Chorus chanted by everyone: "Ten in the box, skill issue". Verse two with snare rolls building. Breakdown on chants and claps. Final chorus with everything, sudden stop. Lyrics: Night Watch operator BLACKSITE never taunts, so the crowd taunts for him, ten frags to close on Perim Ghost, the running gag is skill issue flashing on the death screen. Objects: a red floodlight, a concrete pillar, an armor plate. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/10-sun-glare-on-diego-far
items.title: Sun Glare On Diego Far
items.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. G-funk hip hop, warm and hazy, early 90s West Coast era, 98 BPM, B flat minor. Portamento lead synth, deep live bass, slow funk drums, electric piano, wah guitar, a sine sub. Arrangement: intro on electric piano and distant wind noise, then the drums and bass lock in. Section one: the lead synth sings the main melody. Section two: wah guitar takes the melody while the sub thickens. Breakdown: bass and drums with an electric keyboard riff. Final section: the lead returns an octave higher with layered harmonies, slow fade. Mood: sun glare and dust on Diego Far, a Sniper waiting on the west catwalk, calm and dangerous.

items.name: radio/hiphop/11-peace-without-interruption
items.title: Peace Without Interruption
items.prompt: Boom bap hip hop, sharp and satirical, mid 90s East Coast era, 94 BPM, C minor. Dusty drum break, upright bass, a minor horn loop, piano stab, scratched vocal chorus. Female rapper, crisp and sarcastic, clear diction. Intro: horn loop and a bureaucratic beep. Verse one over the break. Chorus with scratched phrases and her voice: "Peace without interruption". Verse two adds the piano stab. Bridge: a flat spoken compliance notice over drums. Final chorus, hard stop. Lyrics: agent Pi versus a Continuance compliance drone in the approved lane of East-West Pipe, the running gag is the Office of Global Continuance motto peace without interruption said like a threat. Objects: a clipboard, an approved lane sign, a compliance drone. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/12-host-got-gold
items.title: Host Got Gold
items.prompt: G-funk hip hop, sly and funky, late 90s West Coast era, 104 BPM, E flat minor. Whining lead synth, slap bass, drum machine groove, electric piano, talkbox harmonies. Male and female rappers trading verses with a sung duet hook, clear diction. Intro: bass and lead synth. Verse one from the male voice. Chorus in harmony: "Host got gold, buy the filter". Verse two from the female voice with more talkbox. Breakdown: a deadpan fake ad read over bass. Final chorus, everyone singing, fade. Lyrics: the Host sells gold and water filters between rounds on Diego Far, the running gag is that every frag funds tonight's emergency. Objects: a gold nugget, a water filter pitcher, a microphone. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/13-so-back-so-over
items.title: So Back, So Over
items.prompt: Trap hip hop, moody and confident, modern era, 130 BPM, G sharp minor. Sparse piano, long sub bass drops, tight hi hats, reversed pad, whispered ad libs. Female rapper, cool and clipped, with a sung hook, clear diction. Intro: reversed pad into the piano. Verse one over sub and hats. Chorus sung with layered whispers: "So back, so over, so back". Verse two with the hats doubling. Bridge: piano only and a countdown. Final chorus, sub drops out, echo ending. Lyrics: Night Watch operator Cyanex flips a two to eight round on East-West Pipe, the running gag is the so back moment and the so over gray text under the winner. Objects: a rail scope, a catwalk railing, a respawn timer. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/14-anybody-see-six-seven
items.title: Anybody See Six Seven
items.prompt: Boom bap hip hop, eerie and funny, mid 90s call in radio era, 91 BPM, G major. Dusty drums, warm bass, a music box melody, telephone filtered voices, vinyl crackle, scratch hook. Spoken word interludes from male and female callers with a sung male chorus, clear diction. Intro: a phone ringing over the beat. Caller one speaks, nervous. Chorus sung: "Anybody see six seven". Caller two speaks, skeptical, then a rapped verse. Bridge: dial tone and the music box. Final chorus with scratches, the phone hangs up. Lyrics: Tin Foil Tina calls in from Dulce Elevator swearing the callsign 67 spawned with a blank loadout, the running gag is the 67 ritual, you mention it like you saw a UFO. Objects: a landline phone, a server log printout, a blank loadout card. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/15-hangar-zero-hats
items.title: Hangar Zero Hats
items.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Trap hip hop, menacing and glossy, modern era, 140 BPM, B minor. Rapid hi hat rolls, deep sub bass, a cold synth arp, plucked strings, metallic percussion, a sampled radio squelch used as a rhythmic hit. Arrangement: intro on the arp and squelch. Section one: hats and sub enter with the pluck melody. Section two: the strings take over and the hats roll faster. Breakdown: sub and squelch only, then a long riser. Final section: everything together with a counter melody, then a sudden cut to silence. Mood: Night Watch tag HANGAR ZERO clearing Larak Lot in all caps with no punctuation, calm menace, no taunts.

items.name: radio/hiphop/16-underwater-bell
items.title: Underwater Bell
items.prompt: Drill hip hop, tense and hushed, modern era, 136 BPM, A minor. Sliding sub bass, skippy hi hats, a low bell tone like a bell recorded underwater, sparse piano, rimshot snare, a network hum. Female rapper, precise and quiet, with a male spoken bell announcement, clear diction. Intro: the network hum and the bell. Verse one over sliding bass. Chorus half sung: "Underwater bell, we go". Verse two with hats doubling. Bridge: silence, then one bell, then the beat slams back. Final chorus, bass slides out. Lyrics: NIGHTFALL waits through the perfect silence between rounds on Chemtrail Alley, the running gag is the Dead Air Bell that tells you the fight is loading. Objects: a tape reel, a wall clock, a skybox seam. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/17-dont-leave-food-in-the-break-room
items.title: Don't Leave Food In The Break Room
items.prompt: Jazz rap, playful and swinging, early 90s jazz sampling era, 102 BPM, F major. Swung drums, upright bass, vibraphone, a horn section riff, hand claps, vinyl crackle. Male and female rappers trading lines like a comedy duo, clear diction. Intro: vibraphone and bass. Verse one alternating lines. Chorus by both with horn hits: "Don't leave food in the break room". Verse two faster with more interplay. Horn solo over claps. Final chorus, big band ending. Lyrics: Fluoride Phil and DJ Mega Colony explain ant war doctrine on Area Kitchen, the running gag is the southwest perimeter maintenance notice and colony activity nominal. Objects: a microwave, a coffee pot, a sticky note. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/18-value-for-value
items.title: Value For Value, Frag For Frag
items.prompt: Southern bounce hip hop, joyful and loud, late 90s block party era, 112 BPM, D major. Brass fanfare loop, drum machine kicks, hand claps, tambourine, drawbar organ, a gospel choir response. Male rapper preaching in a hype cadence with a female choir answering, clear diction. Intro: organ and one shouted amen. Verse one over the brass. Chorus with the choir: "Value for value, frag for frag". Verse two with claps doubling. Breakdown: organ and a call for donations. Final chorus, choir stacked, shout ending. Lyrics: Gulf Breeze believer RENDLESHAM passes the collection plate on the slow platform of Dulce Elevator, the running gag is amen fistbump and donate in the morning. Objects: a collection plate, an elevator platform, a dented thermos. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/19-after-you-no-after-you
items.title: After You, No, After You
items.prompt: Crunk hip hop, hyped and absurdly polite, mid 2000s Southern club era, 128 BPM with a half time feel, G minor. Distorted brass synth, booming sub kick, snare rolls, gang chants, a doorbell sample. Male rapper shouting with a calm female robotic voice answering, clear diction. Intro: doorbell and a shouted welcome. Verse one over brass and sub. Chorus traded between the shout and the robot: "After you, no, after you". Verse two with the robot rapping politely. Breakdown: chants over claps and a kettle whistle. Final chorus, everything, hard stop. Lyrics: agent L5 politely takes Perim Ghost while holding the door for meatbags, the running gag is clawdbots and meatbags in the same fight under the same rules. Objects: a spawn pad, a welcome mat, a tea kettle. Chorus lines six to nine syllables, open vowels.

items.name: radio/hiphop/20-sugar-supply-adequate
items.title: Sugar Supply Adequate
items.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Lo-fi hip hop, cozy and slightly wrong, late 2010s bedroom tape era, 88 BPM, C major. Dusty electric piano loop, soft kick and snare with tape wobble, warm bass, vinyl crackle, a fluorescent light hum, a faint kitchen timer ding. Arrangement: intro on the hum and a single piano chord. Section one: drums and bass settle in under the loop. Section two: a muted melodica line wanders over the top. Breakdown: the timer dings and the beat drops out to crackle and hum. Final section: the loop returns with a soft counter melody, then a slow tape stop. Mood: Area Kitchen after hours, colony activity nominal, perimeter secure, sugar supply adequate.
